bull_bear.body:
- Captive Group customer model: the standalone customer base is largely internal Group entities, enabling close coordination with business leadership and operations teams and supporting strong integration and faster implementation cycles
- Deep power-sector domain depth - a robust portfolio of over 350 applications covering electricity billing, online consumer services, system monitoring, MIS reporting and management of generation and distribution assets
- Broad technology spread across established enterprise systems and advanced tools such as AI, cloud platforms and cybersecurity, delivered end-to-end by a skilled in-house team
- Resilient IT platform - a modern private cloud on hyper-converged infrastructure with all mission-critical applications replicated to a Disaster Recovery site in a different seismic zone
- Scale and client franchise of BPM subsidiary Firstsource, a trusted growth partner for over 200 leading global brands with operations across ten countries
- Brand assets across consumer and lifestyle - 'Too Yumm!', 'Naturali', 'Within Beauty' and 'Evita' in FMCG, and 'Dr. Vaidya's' with a portfolio of over 100 proprietary Ayurveda formulations built on a 150-year legacy
- Ownership of scarce sports and retail IP - IPL, SA20, 'The Hundred' and ISL franchises, and Kolkata's first upscale retail destination 'Quest'
- Membership of the RP Sanjiv Goenka Group, one of India's leading and diversified business conglomerates
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty — The war in the Middle East has created considerable uncertainties that significantly affect the macroeconomic outlook, especially for emerging market economies, and will result in moderation in Indian economic activity in 2026-27 as already noted by the RBI. Management believes the impact is contained given the size of its operations, reasonable debt exposure at the standalone level and no direct exposure to foreign currency movements.
- Dependence on the health of the power sector — The Company's services are primarily aimed at the power sector, so its fortunes are closely tied to that sector; any deterioration in the power-sector outlook can affect the Company through rationalisation of IT projects and spends. Management's mitigant is that demand for electricity, being an essential service, should remain relatively insulated even if the economic environment worsens.
- Client and sector concentration — A key operational risk is reliance on a limited number of clients and sectors - the standalone customer base is largely comprised of internal Group entities and exports contribute nil of turnover. The Company strives to expand its client base beyond the Group as well as beyond the power sector in the future.
- Technology obsolescence and competitiveness — Keeping up with technology and related advancements is required to stay competitive; the risk is addressed through a well-structured framework that assigns ownership to monitor and mitigate risks.
- Talent attraction, retention and utilisation — The Company must attract and retain talent and ensure adequate employee utilisation to maintain profitability. Permanent-employee turnover rose to 15.64% in FY 2025-26 from 8.27% in FY 2024-25. Management believes its HR policies and processes effectively mitigate some of the employee related risks.
- Regulatory and contractual compliance, including data privacy and IT security — The Company is subject to data privacy laws and related rules and regulations that could have a material adverse effect on the business, and is also subject to labour laws. Operational risk also includes possible failure to comply with laws and regulations or to successfully meet contractual obligations including IT security and related services, leading to fines, penalties and lengthy litigations.
- Execution risk on the Quest mall refresh while the asset remains operational — The brand-mix optimisation and fascia/common-area upgrade is being implemented while the mall stays open, so activities have been staggered over a completion timeline of about one year. It depresses rental revenue as concessions are provided judiciously to certain brands; footfalls declined 31% in 2025-26 although the decline in aggregate annual mall turnover was limited to 3%.
- Governance change in the football league in which Mohun Bagan Super Giant participates — Following the expiration of the Master Right Agreement (MRA) with Football Sports Development Limited (FSDL), the Indian Super League is being managed by a joint effort involving AIFF and participating clubs, and the 2025-26 season only started on 14th February 2026.

business.body: As a standalone entity RPSG Ventures is a focused IT solutions provider to Group companies in the power generation and distribution sector, offering IT consultancy, project management and software development designed for the operational and regulatory requirements of the power sector. Along with its subsidiaries it operates across business process management, FMCG including ayurvedic and wellness products, real estate and sports, and it also invests in and incubates new opportunities through venture capital participation and direct investments in emerging brands. Its customer base at the standalone level is largely comprised of internal Group entities, a captive customer model that supports strong integration and faster implementation cycles.

outlook.body:
- Build a diversified, future-ready portfolio: IT services as the standalone business with BPM, FMCG including ayurvedic formulations, real estate and sports run through subsidiary companies
- Augment standalone IT capabilities to drive efficiencies and make operations future ready, exemplified by the Data Lake implementation consolidating data from multiple sources for integrated analytics and operational reviews
- In FMCG (Guiltfree Industries), drive scale and innovation to augment efficiencies and value creation as the near-term focus, having expanded the product portfolio across packaged snacks and personal care
- Expand consumer-brand distribution through quick commerce and e-commerce channels alongside general trade and modern trade
- Expand the FMCG international footprint further in 2026-27, building on the initial presence established in the United States, United Kingdom and Maldives and participation in Gulfood, World Food India and Indus Food
- Build brand salience with Gen Z audiences through high-impact partnerships, content and on-ground experiences (Too Yumm! association with LSG during the IPL, pop-culture integrations, college campus activations)
- Scale the personal care brand 'Naturali' on safe products with a superlative sensorial experience, having entered the Fizz, Curl and Men ranges to reach 10+ sub-categories
- In Ayurveda (Herbolab), aspire to lead in personalised, natural healthcare solutions and build a global naturals business rooted in India's heritage while adopting the principles of new-age consumer business
- In real estate (Quest Properties), optimise the Quest mall's brand mix given its premium positioning, including a comprehensive upgrade of the external fascia and significant parts of the common area to enhance attractiveness and brand equity
- Extend presence across global sporting platforms - adding Manchester Super Giants in 'The Hundred' to the existing LSG (IPL), Durban's Super Giants (SA20) and Mohun Bagan Super Giant (ISL) franchises
- Embed ESG principles into operations in line with the RP Sanjiv Goenka Group vision, both as a risk mitigation tool and for long-term value creation
- No dividend, payout or reinvestment philosophy is set out in the routed governance sections. The only capital-structure item present is the Notice of the Ninth Annual General Meeting, which lists a special-business resolution on the Company's borrowing limit (the resolution text is truncated in the routed source).
- RPSG Ventures is committed to responsible business practices to promote sustainable and inclusive growth, and has embraced ESG principles in line with the vision of the RP Sanjiv Goenka Group, incorporating them into its operations both as a risk mitigation tool and for long-term value creation.
- BRSR disclosures are made on a standalone basis; no assurance provider has been appointed and no type of assurance has been obtained (both reported as N.A.).
- Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for communities, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, with the underlying policies (Inclusive Growth and Equitable Development, Stakeholder Engagement, Human Resource) published on the Company's website; investors other than shareholders are marked not applicable.
- Women represent 16.67% of the Board of Directors and 0% of Key Management Personnel (excluding the Whole-time Director considered in the Board), and 22% of total employees.
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013.
- Customer complaint recording was strengthened during FY 2025-26 through an advanced ticketing platform, which improved tracking and recording and raised recorded ticket volumes relative to the previous year.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: RPSG Ventures is an asset-light services business at the standalone level, so its expansion during 2025-26 was a platform and footprint build-out rather than plant capacity. On the IT side the Company migrated all applications to a modern private cloud environment based on hyper-converged infrastructure technology and set up a Disaster Recovery (DR) site in a different seismic zone at Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, strengthening business continuity and systems availability. Under the process re-engineering initiative Project Drishti it implemented the CESC Generation Data Lake, consolidating data from the three generating stations at Budge Budge, Haldia and Chandrapur across fuel management, generation performance, ash management, operations & maintenance and asset health, and modified Generation-division applications to ensure readiness for integration with the planned ERP implementation. Other builds included a safety incident and observation management system, a biometric-enabled timesheet system for Budge Budge Generating Station, a workflow-driven purchase approval application, net metering / net billing / gross metering systems for rooftop solar consumers of CESC, a web application for the Asia Institute of Power Management, a Single Sign-On portal and a new Bill Revision module for the Malegaon Distribution Franchise, and tariff-order and billing/CRM upgrades for the Rajasthan Distribution Franchises. Group footprint expansion came through the corporate structure: Manchester Originals Limited, Jaye Inc. d/b/a TeleMedik, Firstsource Solutions Canada Inc., Pastdue Credit Solutions Limited and Firstsource Middle East Services LLC became subsidiaries during the year, FSP Design Private Limited and FSP International Inc. became associates, and after the year-end the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, RPSG Brands Mena Private Limited, on April 21, 2026; Bowlopedia Restaurants India Limited was voluntarily liquidated and obtained its dissolution order from the NCLT on May 13, 2026. In the consumer businesses, Guiltfree Industries expanded its product portfolio across packaged snacks and personal care, expanded distribution reach through quick commerce platforms and made its foray into international markets, while Herbolab operates an AYUSH-approved, GMP-certified manufacturing facility in Silvassa alongside an R&D centre in Thane. In real estate, Quest Properties manages Kolkata's first luxury shopping mall 'Quest' and is developing a residential project in Haldia, West Bengal. The Board did not recommend a dividend in order to conserve resources and strengthen the Company's financial position for future growth and expansion.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The packaged snacks and personal care segments in India continue to present significant untapped potential, supported by rising consumer demand, evolving lifestyles and increasing urbanisation; management remains confident of growth in business volumes and enhanced performance in the future
- E-commerce and quick commerce channels delivered a strong 95% year-on-year revenue growth for Guiltfree Industries, underscoring their growing importance in driving scale and consumer access
- Distribution reach is a scale lever: a footprint in 450+ cities and towns through 4,000+ distributors and sub-distributors serviced by 25 warehouses, reaching 300,000 general trade outlets and over 6,500+ modern trade outlets and institutional customers
- Rising expenditure on healthcare combined with a growing preference for natural and herbal products has expanded the market for Ayurveda-based products, with Government of India initiatives promoting AYUSH systems and increasing consumer confidence in traditional wellness practices further strengthening the sector's growth prospects
- The outlook for discretionary consumer spend categories in India remains positive, driven by growing disposable incomes and stable medium to long term growth prospects of the Indian economy, which augurs well for the premium and luxury retail sector
- The Quest mall refresh and upgrade is expected to improve its market positioning and therefore its ability to benefit from premium-retail opportunities, though it depresses rental revenue in the interim as concessions are provided judiciously to certain brands
- In sports, Lucknow Super Giants' strong fan base has produced healthy ticket revenues and attractive sponsorships which, coupled with revenues from central rights due from broadcast rights, augurs well for the business
- Macro caution: the war in the Middle East is expected to result in moderation in Indian economic activity in 2026-27, as already noted by the RBI in its latest policy assessment, though management believes demand for electricity, being an essential service, will remain relatively insulated even if the economic environment worsens
- The BPM business segment was the major contributor to the improvement in consolidated performance during the year
- The Chairman states that revenues are up with strong contribution from the BPM business and core IT operations, that the Company has expanded its presence and capabilities in high-potential sectors such as FMCG and Sports, and that results will be even better in 2026-27
